"How smart nerds hinder the spread of good ideas", a short story https://t.co/iiE0uwCQ89
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image presents a satirical take on how "smart nerds" can inadvertently hinder the dissemination of valuable ideas. The title, "How smart nerds hinder the spread of good ideas," is prominently displayed in large, dark gray text at the top of the image.
    
    The accompanying text, written in smaller, dark gray font, tells a story about a "smart nerd" who discovers an innovative concept, referred to as "idea X," which is exemplified by "prediction markets." The narrative highlights that while the idea is genuinely useful, it is rejected by the general public due to their dislike of the nerds who promote it. The nerds' cries of "Ad hominem!!!" fall on deaf ears, and the idea is dismissed.
    
    The story takes a turn when, centuries later, a "normie" rediscovers the same idea, rebrands it as "r/agedlikemilk" and "r/agedlikewine," and presents it in a more aesthetically pleasing manner. As a result, the idea gains widespread acceptance and becomes popular.
    
    The final section of the text pokes fun at the nerds, who claim to have been the original proponents of the idea, but are ultimately ignored. The image concludes with the statement, "Each culture gets to write its own history. This is a feature, not a bug." The background of the image is a plain white color.
